G. The Current Status of the Proposal
As of this writing the proposed improvement is scheduled for construction in 1977. There was a public hearing concerning the proposed improvement held on June 20, 1972 at the O.W. Huth Upper Grade Center in Matteson, Illinois, in accordance with the guidelines and Policy and Procedure Memorandums of the Federal Highway Administration in effect at that time.
This improvement is contained in the Northeast Regions five year program. It is anticipated that upon receipt of acceptance of the Final Environmental Statement and Section 4(f) Statement that the Department will proceed with this improvement.
H. General Description of the Surrounding Termain
Significant among the natural environmental factors is the surficial configuration of the terrain. Throughout most of north-eastern Illinois this configuration resulted directly from the geological activities that took place during the Ice Age.
Alternate periods of thawing and freezing during the Ice Age caused the advancing glacier to retreat, then resume its southward thrusts. During its advancing stages the glacier carried with it a sort of debris. During the retreating stages these morainal deposits were left to form part of the existing terrain which, in the Chicago Heights area, is called the Tinley Ground Moraine. The remainder of the terrain is made up by the basin of what once had been Lake Chicago. The basin of this lake (as well as that of present Lake Michigan) was also formed by the glacial activities described above.
The land surface of the area is composed of both Morainal deposits and glacial lake bottom. These two surfaces have different characteristics, especially with respect to drainage patterns, a most important consideration in the process of urbanization.
